messages:
maria: Deploybot auto-paused canary in us-east after T+30m spike — ~5% 500s on /v1/generate. Pausing all queued releases except hotfixes. @alex @sam

 deploy-bot: [ALERT] canary-failure us-east (canary-42). metric: 5.2% 5xx, last 5m. canary traffic redirected to fallback model. auto-pause: true. link: https://deploy.internal/reports/canary-42

 alex: ACK. Do we know if this is a model regression or infra? any recent kernel/quant changes?

 sre-oncall: infra trending: CPU steal on a subset of hosts, but error traces show OOM from model runtime too. I'm spinning up logs + heap dumps. ETA 15m.

 sam: Let's pin current stable model (v2025-03-14-stable) for user traffic and roll canary convo to a rollback candidate. We should block new releases until we confirm. @release-manager

 tia: Agreed. Also need to update release notes / changelog for the teams who had releases scheduled tonight. I'll push a short note to #release-notes.

 maria: Pinning now: run: `./scripts/pin-version --env prod --model v2025-03-14-stable && ./scripts/notify-team --channel=release-team` — done. Can someone confirm traffic is stable?

 deploy-bot: [ACTION] model pinned to v2025-03-14-stable in prod at 1758802472. Canary traffic moved to fallback. All non-critical releases in queue marked PAUSED.

 sre-oncall: Traffic looks nominal after pin. 5xx back to 0.5% in last 3m. Heap dumps collected and uploaded: s3://ci-logs/canary-42/dumps.tar.gz

 sam: OK. We should reschedule deferred releases to the next safe window: Tue 2025-03-18 22:00 UTC (maintenance window). @ops-lead please confirm

 ops-lead: Confirmed. I'll move the windows and notify stakeholders. Anyone needs an earlier emergency slot, ping me.

 tia: I'll update the release notes and add an incident blurb: canary spike -> auto-pause -> pinned stable model. Short CTA for teams to re-run canary after fixes.

 maria: Thanks all. Leaving thread open until SRE posts root cause. If we need rollbacks for specific releases, call it out here.

 sre-oncall: Preliminary root cause: aggressive KV-cache change + one model variant quant tweak causing memory regression under certain load. Will propose revert PR in ~45m.

 sam: If revert patch is ready, let's coordinate canary re-run only after SRE verifies memory profile. No uncoordinated canaries tonight. :thumbsup:

 maria: Noted. Closing active pause once revert merged and canary green. Good job team.
